messages:
Maria C.: hey team — escalated ticket from AcmeCorp. Their batch /rerank call is returning scores that don't line up with per-query candidate lists. customer says items are 'shifted' between queries. seen on prod since ~0900 UTC. attaching payload + response below.

Tom A.: ugh. can you paste the exact request/response? sounds like a classic flattening miscount.

Maria C.: pasted. note we obfuscated keys. request_id: req_0a1b2c3d.

Maria C.: ```json
{
  "queries": [
    {"id": "q1", "text": "best running shoes"},
    {"id": "q2", "text": "trail shoes for wet"}
  ],
  "candidates": [
    {"id": "c1", "text": "Nike Air"},
    {"id": "c2", "text": "Asics Road"},
    {"id": "c3", "text": "Salomon Trail"},
    {"id": "c4", "text": "Merrell Wet Grip"}
  ],
  "per_query_candidate_counts": [2, 2],
  "options": {"return_scores": true}
}
```

Maria C.: response (trimmed): ```json
{
  "request_id": "req_0a1b2c3d",
  "results": [
    {"query_id": "q1", "ranks": [{"candidate_id": "c1", "score": 0.82}, {"candidate_id": "c3", "score": 0.79}]},
    {"query_id": "q2", "ranks": [{"candidate_id": "c2", "score": 0.75}, {"candidate_id": "c4", "score": 0.73}]}
  ]
}
```

Maria C.: note how q1 got c3 (which belongs to q2 according to the per_query counts) — they expect q1->(c1,c2) and q2->(c3,c4).

Sri P.: thanks. quick sanity: per_query_candidate_counts is [2,2] and candidates length=4 so counts sum matches. this smells like an indexing bug when we compute start/end offsets. can you attach server-side request log (the raw flattened indices) and the model's logits?

Maria C.: pasted log excerpt from our proxy: ```
[INFO] 2025-03-12T09:03:21Z request_id=req_0a1b2c3d flattened_candidate_ids=[c1,c2,c3,c4] per_query_counts=[2,2] offsets=[0,2]
[DEBUG] 2025-03-12T09:03:21Z scoring_slice_for_query0 indices=[0,2] -> returning candidates [c1,c3]
```

Tom A.: aha offsets computed as start indices but the end index calc looks wrong. the debug shows "indices=[0,2]" for query0 meaning it's picking positions 0 and 2 (step 2?) instead of 0,1. maybe we used stride logic for interleaved batches somewhere. any recent change in packing logic?

Jack N. (oncall): deploying a rollback patch to the packer yesterday at 08:50 UTC. patch id: packer-fix-20250311. could be related.

support-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-312 (priority P2) — assigned to eng-ml.

Sri P.: thanks @Jack. i'm going to try to reproduce locally. Maria, can you also run a minimal repro with 3 queries where counts = [1,2,1] and verify whether the pattern is interleaving rather than contiguous slices?

Maria C.: running now. reproduction script (curl):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank/batch -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"queries":[{"id":"q1"},{"id":"q2"},{"id":"q3"}],"candidates":[{"id":"a"},{"id":"b"},{"id":"c"},{"id":"d"}],"per_query_candidate_counts":[1,2,1]}'
```

Maria C.: response -> q1 got [a,c], q2 got [b,d], q3 got [b] 

Tom A.: yep that's interleaving: index calculation used a stride equal to num_queries when it should be contiguous. looks like new packer introduced an optimization for column-major flattening for GPU kernels and accidentally flipped behavior for this endpoint.

Sri P.: root cause hypothesis: packer now outputs candidates in column-major for multi-query scoring to optimize memory coalescing. consumer of the flattened array expected row-major. the endpoint's parser didn't update.

Maria C.: customer is upset because they re-ranked wrongly in prod for ~45 minutes and then retried, causing duplicate billing events. billing-bot flagged a spike.

billing-bot: Billing alert: anomalous token usage for account acme-789 between 09:00-09:50 UTC. Estimated extra cost: $120.

Jack N.: i'll quiesce the packer version and route new requests to older image until we ship a proper fix. can we also offer creds credit?

Tom A.: temporary mitigation: validate that per_query_candidate_counts mapping aligns with candidates length and add a strict sanity check in the API: compute expected indices both row-major and column-major; if they disagree, return 400 with helpful message. i'll open a PR for the check.

Sri P.: working on deterministic unit test that covers counts permutations and the packing modes. will also update docs to state expected flattening order.

Maria C.: customer wants repro steps + ETA. what's the timeline?

Jack N.: rollback done. old packer image serving. monitoring shows failure rate drop to 0. still need an eng fix and tests. estimated 4-8 hours to fully patch+deploy.

Tom A.: PR: github.com/redwood/packers/pull/412 — adds validation + toggles to preserve row-major packing for API consumers. requesting review from @Sri P.

Sri P.: will review now. also adding migration script to convert any queued flattened payloads in the pipeline (just in case).

Maria C.: i'll send customer a clear summary and offer a $150 credit for the duplicate runs. i'll include repro and the rollback note. any suggested wording?

Tom A.: say: apology, root cause (packer column-/row-major mismatch after recent deploy), rollback performed at 09:11 UTC, fix in progress with tests, recommended workaround: pin packer to previous image or validate per_query_candidate_counts client-side. offer credit. :thumbsup:

Maria C.: thanks. i'm updating the ticket and closing the support thread once fix merged.

Sri P.: post-mortem item: add an automated fuzz test for per_query_candidate_counts permutations and make packing order explicit in API schema.

Jack N.: tagging ops to run a quick sweep for other endpoints that consume flattened arrays.

support-bot: Incident INC-2025-312 status: resolved -> monitoring.

Maria C.: closing internal thread. follow-up: add docs example showing `per_query_candidate_counts` and mapping to candidate slices.
